text:
maya: Quick question from tabletop: should we rate-limit lease handoffs to avoid mass cross-region traffic during a multi-tenant event?

trent: Yes. If N tenants move in T seconds we should gate handoffs with a token-bucket per-region. Otherwise remote primaries can get hammered.

sofia: Proposal: region-handshake-rate = 50/s default, per-tenant burst=2, global backpressure=true. Also add a fast-path for dedicated tenants with reserved tokens.

maya: How do we surface graceful degradation to callers? We should return clear headers and an HTTP 429 style when handoff is delayed.

ops-bot: experiment.flag created: feature/handshake-rate-limiter -> staging (10%).

trent: Telemetry: emit handshake.queue_depth, handshake.throttled=true/false, handshake.delay_ms. Dashboards per-region.

sofia: Also ensure the control-plane honors lease intent ordering: queued handoffs must be persisted so we don't lose intent after leader failover. Persist to append-only ops-log.

maya: Edge case: if rate limit causes prolonged denial for strict-residency tenants, fallback to local-readonly or 503 depending on tenant policy. Add residency.audit when we serve degraded.

trent: I'll PR rate-limiter + token-bucket + queues + metrics. Sofia, can you own ops-log durability checks?

sofia: Yep. I'll add tests simulating 5k tenants switching and ensure queue stays stable and no remote overload in the sim.

maya: Thanks — sounds like a plan. We'll review metrics after the staging canary.
